traceability.notes:
The story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented.
Core functionality is provided by src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts together with src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts. The rule attaches listeners to all significant branch node types (if, switch cases, try/catch, loops) and, for each visited node, gathers associated comments and checks for @story and @req annotations. Missing annotations are reported via a dedicated message (`missingAnnotation`) that clearly states which annotation is missing, and auto-fix behavior inserts sensible placeholders for the first missing @story and for @req where appropriate.
The helpers implement configuration validation (branchTypes), comment association (via getCommentsBefore and a specialized SwitchCase line-scan), annotation parsing via regex, and controlled auto-fix insertion points based on indentation and start-of-line positions. This design naturally supports nested branches and complex control flow, since it relies solely on each node’s own location and leading comments, not on a particular nesting shape.
Tests in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts comprehensively cover all supported branch types with both annotated and unannotated examples, as well as configuration scenarios including custom branchTypes and invalid types. Additional unit tests in tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts verify configuration handling and error reporting for invalid branchTypes. All of these tests are explicitly tied to this story via @story annotations and pass in the full Jest run.
User-facing documentation for the rule is present in docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md, linked back to this story and requirements. It describes behavior, configuration, and provides correct/incorrect examples and invalid-configuration examples, fulfilling the documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the implemented rule, helpers, tests, plugin integration, and docs—and the fact that all related tests pass—the acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied.
